items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: that's where I had a chance to first hear Earl Hines at the Apex Club, playing piano with Jimmy Noone.

ctx.x: She went and joined Earl Hines' band. We heard her in Cincinnati, brought her back to St. Louis, had Chester Lane to write You Go To My Head, made several arrangements behind her. We took her downtown to a wholesale house where she could buy four or five little evening dresses. They were cheap. But things were rough back in those days. People weren't wearing $100 dresses back in those days. And this was a wholesale place, and she was -- she got to be a Miss Any. (Unintelligible) She was real popular. People were…
Then she started making a little money on the intermissions.

items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: And there were various couples, you know what I mean, they would do cake walk dancing, Professor.

ctx.x: advance, and she'd let you rehearse and prepare for it, see. But then I got so I could read with this group. And we would go to Hot Springs, Arkansas. And this I want to will tell you, because they didn't have nightclubs back in that day. And here's what they would do.

In the wintertime rich people would come to Hot Springs. I can remember Babe Ruth would come down to Hot Springs in the wintertime. And the millionaires would come down. And what they would do, we would play a dance at the Pythiqn Bath House, and all of these whites would come over to the Pythiqn Bath House. And the promoter (unintelligible) would feature cake walking, a dancers' forum dance (unintelligible). And there were various couples, you know what I mean, they would do cake walk dancing, Professor. And…

There was a tune written like this (sings). And the cake walk they would -- you would walk fast like that. They would bend down and you bow, and they had the long dresses, you know, and they had the big hats, you know. And the woman moment would grab the her partner's arms, you know. And they would skip through, you know. And that was the cake walk.
